subject: validator: support including validator context when reporting errors (#2089)
message:
validator: support including validator context when reporting errors (#2089)

* validator: support including validator context when reporting errors

Motivation:

When validating JSON, the `linkml-validate` command builds a JSON Schema
against which the JSON input is checked.  If there are validation
problems, the command prints a single line for each such problem.

In some cases, the failing node is a composition (`allOf`, `anyOf`,
`oneOf`) and the resulting error message is currently rather vague.

Modification:

Update the `ValidationResult` class to include a List of strings.  These
are the validation errors that led to the composition failing.

Note, these contextual failures could (themselves) have further
contextual failures, forming a tree.  In the interests of keeping the
patch small, this change records only the next level; however, a future
patch may address this issue.

The error output is updated to support providing the validation error's
context as lines starting `[CONTEXT]`.

The command-line arguments are updated to support the `-v`/`--verbose`
flag.  Specifying this flag results in the validator printing any
validation error context.

Note, support for the `-v` flag was included for backwards
compatibility; however, it may be acceptable to print the validation
error's context unconditionally.  If so, a future patch could remove
this flag.

Result:

`linkml-validate` now supports the `-v`/`--verbose` option.  Specifying
this option will result in certain validation error reports containing
more information.

Closes: #2088

subject: Improve logging by replacing the use of the root logger by module-level loggers (#2323)
message:
Improve logging by replacing the use of the root logger by module-level loggers (#2323)

* Replace use of the root logger with module-leve loggers

* Replace default logger in `linkml.utils.generator.Generator`

Instead of using the root logger as the default, use a logger
with a name of the class name prepended by the module name.

* Replace default logger in `linkml.utils.schemaloader.SchemaLoader`

Instead of using a logger with a name of the class name as the default,
use a logger with a name of the class name prepended by the module name.
This way allows easier location of  the origin a log message.

* Use module-level logger as default logger for `Generator`

Doing it this way will make logger hierarchy identical to
the Python package hierarchy,
https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html#logger-objects.

* Use module-level logger as default logger for `SchemaLoader`

Doing it this way will make logger hierarchy identical to
the Python package hierarchy,
https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html#logger-objects.

subject: feat(graphql): add support for enumerations (#2303)
message:
feat(graphql): add support for enumerations (#2303)

* feat(graphql): add support for enumerations

Generation of GraphQL enumerations based on those enumerations defined
in the LinkML schema was missing.

LinkML supports enumeration names and permissible values in a format
that is not compabtible with GraphQL. This patch adds the needed
conversions to make them compabible. A dedicated class is added to
handle it in a generic way that can be reused in other parts of LinkML.

Automatic conversion can be disabled with the flag `--strict`.

Enumerations not using `permissible_values` but `reachable_from` to
specify the enumeration permissible values are not supported yet by the
generator. A warning is raised and the enumeration is ignored if this
happens.

Signed-off-by: ufed62fd9d5116ced <ufed62fd9d5116ced@users.invalid>

Enhance OWL enum/permissible value handling and add comprehensive test coverage

This commit improves the OWL generator's handling of permissible values and enums,
with better type mapping support and comprehensive test coverage for different
OWL representation strategies.

## Changes

### linkml/generators/owlgen.py
- Add support for owl: and rdfs: prefixed default permissible value types in `_permissible_value_owl_type_for()`
- Add metadata handling for enum definitions via `add_metadata()` call in `_add_enum()`
- Add metadata handling for individual permissible value nodes when they are URIRefs
- Improve type signature of `add_metadata()` to accept PermissibleValue objects
- Add clarifying comment about non-null PV validation logic

### tests/test_generators/test_owlgen.py
- Add comprehensive parameterized test `test_permissible_values()` covering:
  - Different default permissible value types (owl:Class, rdfs:Literal, owl:NamedIndividual)
  - Per-PV type overrides via implements field
  - Mixed URI/non-URI permissible value scenarios
- Add detailed docstring documenting OWL mapping strategies and expected behaviors
- Add PermissibleValueURIMixture enum for test parameterization
- Test validates correct owl:unionOf vs owl:oneOf usage based on PV types

### linkml/utils/schema_builder.py
- Fix bug in `add_enum()` where PermissibleValue objects weren't being added to enum definition

## Related Issues
- Addresses TODO comments in owlgen.py lines 668, 929, 1186, 1205 regarding enum mapping
- References https://github.com/linkml/linkml/issues/1841 for complex enum constraints

The test suite now comprehensively validates that:
- owl:Class permissible values generate owl:unionOf expressions with URIRef elements
- rdfs:Literal permissible values generate owl:oneOf expressions with Literal elements
- owl:NamedIndividual permissible values generate owl:oneOf expressions with URIRef elements
- Mixed type scenarios work correctly or are skipped when undefined

Inlined classes without an identifier are typically inlined as a list,
because it is unclear what to use as key. This patch sets that default.

This applies to the cases where `inlined: True` has been explicitly set.
But also to those were it has been automatically set, because no value
was assigned and inlining was the only possiblity.

subject: pydanticgen: make the default for optional list configurable
message:
pydanticgen: make the default for optional list configurable

Historical behaviour for optional lists in pydantic was to initialise them with None. However, https://github.com/linkml/linkml/pull/2877 changed
this behaviour to empty list. This caused regressions for us (see example below). This patch makes the behaviour of pydantic for optional lists configurable,
so we can restore the old behaviour.

Test case:

```
  AssociatedNetElement:
    description: >-
      A RSM Associated Net Element
    attributes:
      netElement:
        range: PositioningNetElement
        inlined: false
      bounds:
        range: float
        multivalued: true
        minimum_cardinality: 1
        maximum_cardinality: 2
      appliesInDirection:
        range: string
      lateralPosition:
        range: string # FIXME custom class LateralPosition instead of str in RSM
```

After PR #2877 AssociatedNetElement() will raise an error (validation fails because altough `bounds` is not required, when it is filled in, the cardinality is mandatory).

subject: Fix SHACL generator to use rdfs:comment for NodeShape descriptions (#3061)
message:
Fix SHACL generator to use rdfs:comment for NodeShape descriptions (#3061)

* Fix SHACL generator to use rdfs:comment for NodeShape descriptions

Per the SHACL spec, sh:description has rdfs:domain of sh:PropertyShape,
so using it on NodeShapes causes RDFS-aware validators to incorrectly
infer the NodeShape is also a PropertyShape.

This changes NodeShape descriptions to use rdfs:comment instead, while
keeping sh:description for PropertyShapes (which is correct per spec).

Fixes #3059

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix ruff formatting in test file

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Also fix sh:name to use rdfs:label for NodeShape titles

Per reviewer feedback from @h9a7e5d7f89ca8dcd, sh:name also has rdfs:domain
of sh:PropertyShape, causing the same RDFS inferencing issue.

Changes:
- NodeShape titles: sh:name → rdfs:label
- NodeShape descriptions: sh:description → rdfs:comment (previous commit)
- PropertyShape titles/descriptions: unchanged (sh:name/sh:description correct per spec)

subject: Add support for "true enums" in OO code generator.
message:
Add support for "true enums" in OO code generator.

Add a new boolean option `true_enums` to the OOCodeGenerator class. When
enabled, the generator will treat each enumeration as its own distinct
type. This means that for each enumeration:

(a) specific code should be generated to represent that enumeration, using
whatever mechanism exists in the underlying language to represent
enumerated types (e.g. `enum` in Java);

(b) slots whose range is set to that enumeration will be typed as being
of the generated enum type, rather than being string-typed.

Subclasses and users of OOCodeGenerator will obviously need to be
updated to cope with the fact that the `create_documents()` method will
now return a document for every enum in addition to a document for every
class.

For that reason, the new behaviour is disabled by default.

subject: Add support for true enums in the Java generator.
message:
Add support for true enums in the Java generator.

Adapt the Java code generator to use the newly added support for "true
enumerations" in the OOCodeGenerator class. Both the default template
and the record-based template are updated to cope with the possibility
that the document for which they are supposed to generate code might
contain an enumeration type rather than a class.

The support for "true enumerations" is disabled by default for backwards
compatibility. It has to be explicitly enabled with the `--true-enums`
option.

subject: Add subproperty_of support to generators (#3065)
message:
Add subproperty_of support to generators (#3065)

* Add subproperty_of support to pydanticgen

Implement Phase 1 of subproperty_of constraint expansion for pydanticgen.
When a slot has subproperty_of set, the generator now constrains valid
values to the referenced slot and all its descendants (via is_a).

Changes:
- Add _generate_subproperty_constraint() method to collect slot descendants
- Add _format_slot_value_for_range() to format values by range type:
  - uriorcurie/curie: CURIEs (e.g., biolink:related_to)
  - uri: full URIs
  - string/other: snake_case slot names
- Modify generate_python_range() to check subproperty_of
- Add expand_subproperty_of flag (default True) to disable if needed
- Add 7 unit tests covering hierarchy, formatting, and validation
- Add documentation section in docs/generators/pydantic.rst

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add subproperty_of support to jsonschemagen

- Add expand_subproperty_of flag (default True) to enable/disable feature
- Add _format_slot_value_for_range() helper to format values by range type
  (CURIE for uriorcurie, full URI for uri, snake_case for string)
- Add _get_subproperty_values() helper to collect slot descendants
- Modify get_value_constraints_for_slot() to generate enum constraints
- Add CLI option --expand-subproperty-of/--no-expand-subproperty-of
- Add 7 unit tests covering hierarchy, formatting, and validation

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add subproperty_of support to shaclgen

- Add `_get_subproperty_values()` method to collect slot descendants
- Add `_add_subproperty_constraint()` to create sh:in constraints
- Modify slot processing to check `subproperty_of`
- Use URIRef for URI-like ranges, Literal for string ranges
- Add `expand_subproperty_of` flag (default `True`) to disable if needed
- Add CLI option `--expand-subproperty-of/--no-expand-subproperty-of`
- Add 6 unit tests covering hierarchy, formatting, and validation

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add subproperty_of support to shexgen

- Add `_get_subproperty_values()` method to collect slot descendants
- Modify `visit_class_slot()` to create NodeConstraint values for subproperty_of
- Use SchemaView to resolve slot hierarchy
- Format values as full URIs for ShEx compatibility
- Add `expand_subproperty_of` flag (default `True`) to disable if needed
- Add CLI option `--expand-subproperty-of/--no-expand-subproperty-of`
- Add 4 unit tests covering hierarchy, disable flag, and slot_usage

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add subproperty_of support to typescriptgen

- Add `_get_subproperty_union_type()` method to collect slot descendants
- Modify `range()` to generate TypeScript union types for subproperty_of
- Format values as CURIEs for URI-like ranges, snake_case for string ranges
- Add `expand_subproperty_of` flag (default `True`) to disable if needed
- Add CLI option `--expand-subproperty-of/--no-expand-subproperty-of`
- Add 5 unit tests covering hierarchy, formatting, disable flag, and slot_usage

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add subproperty_of support to rustgen

When a slot has subproperty_of set, the rustgen now generates a Rust enum
with variants for all slot descendants. Values are formatted according to
the slot's range type:
- uri/uriorcurie ranges: CURIEs (e.g., "biolink:causes")
- string ranges: snake_case slot names (e.g., "causes")

Key changes:
- Added expand_subproperty_of flag (default True) to RustGenerator
- Added _get_subproperty_enum() to generate Rust enums for constrained slots
- Added _get_range_info_with_subproperty() to wrap range info with enum types
- Modified generate_attribute() to use enum types for subproperty_of slots
- Updated gen_poly_trait() to use subproperty-aware range info
- Updated get_rust_range_info_across_descendants() to handle enum types
- Added 5 unit tests covering basic usage, deep hierarchies, string ranges,
  disable option, and cargo check validation

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add compliance tests for subproperty_of constraint

Adds comprehensive compliance tests to verify subproperty_of behavior
across all generators. Tests cover:

- Basic value constraint (valid values from hierarchy, invalid values rejected)
- Range type formatting (string vs uriorcurie)
- Deep hierarchy support (4 levels)
- slot_usage narrowing behavior
- Multivalued slot support

Tests verify that pydantic, jsonschema, shacl, and shex generators
correctly implement the constraint, while other generators are marked
as INCOMPLETE.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Refactor subproperty_of utilities into shared module

Extract common subproperty_of handling code from 6 generators into a
shared module at generators/common/subproperty.py. This consolidates:
- CURIE_TYPES and URI_TYPES constants
- is_uri_range() and is_curie_range() helper functions
- format_slot_value_for_range() for range-type-aware formatting
- get_subproperty_values() for collecting slot hierarchy values

Reduces code duplication by ~90 lines while maintaining identical
functionality across pydanticgen, jsonschemagen, shaclgen, shexgen,
typescriptgen, and rustgen.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Update biolink snapshots for subproperty_of support

The jsonschemagen and shexgen now generate enum constraints for slots
with subproperty_of, which affects biolink-model's predicate slots that
use subproperty_of in slot_usage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix broken link to javagen.py in docs

Update path to reflect monorepo structure.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Fix circular dependency in metamodel versioning (#3079)
message:
Fix circular dependency in metamodel versioning (#3079)

* Set metamodel_version only if not already defined

Updates rawloader.py to assign metamodel_version only when the schema does not already specify one. This allows schemas to define their own version, such as the metamodel itself, instead of inheriting from the runtime.

* Use schema's metamodel_version in JSON Schema output

Replaces the global metamodel_version reference with self.schema.metamodel_version when generating JSON Schema, ensuring the correct version is used for each schema instance.

* Add tests for metamodel_version preservation in schema loader

Introduces tests to verify that metamodel_version is preserved when explicitly defined in a schema and set from the runtime when not defined. Addresses issue #2719 to prevent overwriting user-defined metamodel_version, ensuring correct behavior for metamodel generation.

* Set metamodel_version in Generator if undefined

Ensures that the schema's metamodel_version is set to the current metamodel_version if it is not already defined. This change maintains consistency with SchemaLoader-based generators.

subject: Refactor the Java code generator to allow “template variants” (#3124)
message:
Refactor the Java code generator to allow “template variants” (#3124)

* Introduce the notion of "template variants" for the Java generator.

This PR refactors the Java code generator to make it possible to have an
arbitrary number of "template variants", where a variant can be used to
represent a particular "style" of Java code.

This replaces the previous code that was used to implement the
`--generate-records` option by a more generic mechanism.

There is no longer a default template that is embedded directly into the
code of the Java generator module. Instead, all templates, for all
variants, are expected to be located in the `javagen` directory, and
named according to the following convention:

  NAME[-VARIANT].jinja2

where NAME is the name of the class or enum to be generated (can be
`class` for a generic template to use for all classes, or `enum` for a
generic template to use for all enums) and VARIANT is an optional
variant name.

When the generator has to generate the code file for a class named
`Foo` using the variant `bar`, it will successively search for the
following templates, using the first one that is found:

  1. Foo-bar.jinja2 (template specific for the Foo class, bar variant);
  2. class-bar.jinja2 (generic class template, bar variant);
  3. Foo.jinja2 (template specific for the Foo class, default variant);
  4. class.jinja2 (generic class template, default variant).

Steps 1 and 2 are skipped if no explicit variant is requested.

The same logic applies when generating the code for an enum (assuming
the `--true-enums` option is used), with the fallback templates in step
2 and 4 being named `enum-bar.jinja2` and `enum.jinja2` in that case.

On the command line, two new options are added:

  * `--template-dir` to specify an alternative directory for the
    templates;
  * `--template-variant` to specify the variant to use.

The existing option `--generate-records` is kept for backwards
compatibility, and is now equivalent to `--template-variant=records`.

The `--template-file` option can still be used to completely bypass the
template selection mechanism and use a single template for all the
objects to generate.

* Add test for `--template-file` option of the Java code generator.

Add a test to check that we can still use the `--template-file` option
of the Java code generator and get the expected results, bypassing the
generator's own logic to pick up the template.

* Fix missing newlines.

1. Damn "modern" editors.
2. Why isn't that check part of `uv run tox -e lint`?

subject: javagen: Represent boolean slots as Boolean-typed fields by default.
message:
javagen: Represent boolean slots as Boolean-typed fields by default.

This commit applies to boolean-typed slots the same logic that is
already used to number-typed slots: by default, we render the slot as a
"boxed" boolean type (`Boolean`) rather than as a primitive type
(`boolean`), unless the slot is required.

This is because, if the slot is optional, then there may be cases when
the client code (the code that will be built upon the generated code)
will need to know whether a boolean-typed slot has been explicitly set
to a value or not. This is not possible using the primitive `boolean`
type, which in Java only accepts `true` or `false` -- there is no way to
record any kind of "unset/unknown" value. Using a boxed boolean (which
is basically an `Object` holding a boolean value) fixes that problem:
since it is an `Object`, any variable or field holding this type of
value can hold a `null` reference, explicitly indicating that the
variable or field has not been set.

closes #3176

Add two boolean flags to OwlSchemaGenerator:

- skip_min_zero_cardinality_axioms: suppresses owl:minCardinality 0
  restrictions, which are satisfied by every individual and carry no
  information.
- skip_vacuous_local_range_axioms: suppresses owl:allValuesFrom
  restrictions whose filler is either owl:Thing or the same URI as the
  property's globally declared rdfs:range (fully entailed, hence
  vacuous).  Attribute slots, which have no global rdfs:range, are
  unaffected.

that class-level attribute slots are not mistakenly treated as top-level
slots with a global range.

Expose both options as CLI flags.

subject: feat(plantumlgen): add --include-enums flag to render enum definitions
message:
feat(plantumlgen): add --include-enums flag to render enum definitions

When --include-enums is set, the PlantUML generator now:

- Emits a PlantUML `enum` block for each enumeration referenced by a
  slot in the generated classes.  Each permissible value is listed as a
  member; values with a `meaning` URI show it in brackets.
- Emits `<|--` generalisation arrows for enum `inherits` relationships
  (only between enums that are themselves rendered).
- Emits `-->` association arrows from each class to its enum-typed slots,
  scoped to slots directly owned by the class (via `domain_of`) to avoid
  duplicate arrows for inherited slots.

By default the flag is False, so existing behaviour is unchanged.

The module-level `pytestmark` in test_plantuml.py no longer includes
`pytest.mark.docker`; that mark is now applied directly to the three
tests that require a running Docker/Kroki container.

Adds an `include_all` field and `--all / -a` CLI option to
`PlantumlGenerator`.  When set, every class and every enumeration in the
schema is rendered, regardless of any explicit `--classes` selection and
without needing to pass `--include-enums` separately.

Previously, visit_schema() always returned @startuml/@enduml text when
no --directory was given, regardless of --format.  The Kroki URL also
hardcoded /plantuml/svg/ even when a different format was requested.

* Fix Kroki URL to use self.format for rendered formats (svg, png, …)
  and fall back to svg only for text formats (puml, plantuml).
* For stdout without --directory: text formats still return PlantUML
  source; svg/json fetch from Kroki and return the response text;
  binary formats (png, pdf, jpg) raise ValueError pointing to
  --directory.
* Fix copy-paste bug in directory file_suffix that checked "puml" twice.

subject: feat(plantumlgen): add --mark-mixins flag for visual mixin distinction
message:

Adds a mark_mixins field and --mark-mixins/--no-mark-mixins CLI option.
When enabled, mixin classes receive a <<(M,orchid) mixin>> PlantUML spot
stereotype so they are visually distinguishable from regular classes.
The spot notation overrides `hide circle`, giving mixin boxes a coloured
"M" marker analogous to the "E" marker PlantUML adds to enum blocks.

subject: fix(plantumlgen): render mixin relationships as dashed specialisation arrows
message:
fix(plantumlgen): render mixin relationships as dashed specialisation arrows

Replace the plain association arrow ("-- : uses") for mixin relationships
with a dashed generalisation/realization arrow (^..) so the diagram reads
naturally: mixin (parent) on the left, user class (child) on the right.

This matches standard UML where interface/mixin realisation uses a dashed
hollow-triangle arrow, while direct is-a inheritance uses a solid one (^--),
making the two inheritance flavours visually distinct at a glance.

fix(shaclgen): migrate ShaclGenerator from SchemaLoader to SchemaView (#3293)

ShaclGenerator was stuck in an inconsistent state: it set
uses_schemaloader=True but created a SchemaView in __post_init__
before calling super(). The parent Generator.__post_init__ then
ran _initialize_using_schemaloader(), which overwrote self.schema,
self.base_dir and self.importmap — discarding the SchemaView's
import resolution context.

This caused cross-directory imports via importmap to fail with
doubled paths (e.g. linkml/linkml/schema.yaml) because the
SchemaLoader re-derives base_dir from the schema file path.

Fix: set uses_schemaloader=False and let Generator.__post_init__
create the SchemaView with the correct importmap and base_dir
parameters.  This aligns with the documented migration plan (#923)
and the pattern used by 13 other generators (docgen, owlgen,
excelgen, jsonschemagen, etc.).

Includes a regression test for cross-directory imports via importmap
that verifies shapes from both the main schema and the imported
subdirectory schema are present in the SHACL output.

Fixes #2913

subject: Misc improvements to the Java code generator (#3255)
message:
Misc improvements to the Java code generator (#3255)

* Use `java.time.LocalTime` to represent `xsd:time`.

The base `xsd:time` type is intended to represent a date-less time (as
in `07:30:25`). The Java `java.time.Instant` class is _not_ suitable for
this usage -- it is intended to represent a completely precise point in
time, including the date.

The best option to represent a time and _only a time_ in Java is the
`java.time.LocalTime` class, which we uses here.

Of note, the Java class only allows zone-less time, contrary to the
Python `datetime.time.fromisoformat` method (which underpins the Python
implementation of that type). I do not consider that as a great concern
as representing a zoned time without any date information should be
pointless anyway -- if you need to record a point in time with enough
precision that you also need to know the timezone, you probably need a
full datetime rather than a simple time.

closes #3213

* javagen: Fix rendering of `linkml:Any`.

A class marked with the URI `linkml:Any` is intended to represent
literally anything. That is, a slot with a range set to the `linkml:Any`
class can hold any kind of object.

However, the Java code generator is not aware of that meaning, and
dutifully treat the `linkml:Any` class as merely any other LinkML class.

That is, given the following definitions:

```
classes:
  AnyObject:
    class_uri: linkml:Any

  Foo:
    attributes:
      anything:
        range: AnyObject
```

the Java code generator will produce the following:

```
public class AnyObject { }

public class Foo {
  private AnyObject anything;
}
```

Java's strict typing rules will then ensure that _nothing_ can ever be
stored in the `Foo#anything` slot, thereby achieving the exact opposite
of what the schema author intended. In order to be able to store
anything, the slot should be typed as Object (and the `AnyObject` class
does not need to be generated at all).

So, the Java generator must be given the opportunity to recognise the
`linkml:Any` class and tweak the OODocument objects accordingly.

This commit does that by adding a `map_class(ClassDefinition)` method to
the OOCodeGenerator class, allowing any derived class to map a LinkML
class to a pre-existing (non-LinkML-derived) class. The Java code
generator overrides this method to map the `linkml:Any` class to the
standard Java Object class.

closes #3177

* Render `uri`-typed slots as URI fields.

Slots typed as `uri` are currently rendered as String-typed fields, but
Java has a dedicated URI type that we can use.

* Make sure all types are imported.

Amend the Java code templates to make sure they import the URI,
LocalDate, LocalTime, and ZonedDateTime classes, which are not in Java's
default namespace.

* oocodegen: Provide URIs for the classes, slots, and enums.

This commit amends the OOClass, OOField, and OOEnum classes in the
oocodegen module so that they include a field containing the URI
associated with the LinkML class, slot, and enum, respectively.

This is so these URIs can be obtained from within the Jinja2 templates.
A soon-to-be-proposed new template variant for the Java code generator
will need access to these URIs.

* gen-java: Add `--extra-template` option.

This commit adds a new `--extra-template` option to the Java code
generator.

The rationale for this is that users might want/need to generate more
code from the model than just the code for the classes and enums. For
example, one might want to generate some kind of helper methods to work
with the model-derived classes.

The CLI method simply passes the list of extra templates to the
JavaGenerator#serialize() method, which will then, for each extra
template, create a "pseudo OODocument" that is then serialised as any
other OODocument -- except that this OODocument contains neither a class
nor an enum.

This assumes that, for each additional template Foo requested, a
template named `Foo.jinja2` does exist in the template directory.
Providing that template is the user's responsibility.

Of note, we now pass the entire JavaGenerator object to the Jinja
template engine. This is so the template can access the generator and
particularly its `schemaview` object, so that it can query the schema as
needed to generate whatever needs to be generated.

* java-gen: Allow to generate visitor interfaces.

This commit adds a `--visitor` option to the Java generator to easily
generate visitor interfaces. This may be particularly useful when
working with models when a given class has a lot of (direct or indirect)
children, like in the KGCL model where the `Change` class has more than
50 descendants.

Asking for a `Foo` visitor (with `--visitor Foo`, and assuming that
`Foo` is the name of a class in the model) will:

(1) insert into the code for the Foo class and into the code for all its
descendants an `accept(IFooVisitor)` method;

(2) create an `IFooVisitor` interface with `visit()` methods for the Foo
class and all its descendants.

The code of the visitor interface is generated from the new template
type `_visitor`. As for the other template types (class and enum),
variants may also exist in the template directory.

closes #1449

* Avoid name clashes with Java keywords.

When generating the "safe name" for classes and slots in the generic
OOCodeGenerator, add a step where we give the derived generator for a
given language a chance to check whether the "safe name" would clash
with a reserved keyword in that language, and provide an alternative
name in such a case.

Used only by the Java code generator for now (where the alternative
proposed in the event of a clash is simply the initial name with an
appended underscore).

* gen-java: Allow generating code suitable for incenp.org's LinkML-Java.

The LinkML-Java runtime library at
https://github.org/gouttegd/linkml-java requires that the Java code it
will work with be annotated with specific annotations, that the runtime
can use to obtain schema-derived informations that it would have no way
to obtain otherwise (except by having a runtime copy of the original
schema -- a need we would like to avoid).

This commit therefore adds a new template variant, `org.incenp.linkml`,
specifically intended to generate code that is directly usable by the
LinkML-Java runtime.

This requires adding a few helper methods in the `javagen.py` module
that can be used from within the template, but apart from that, all the
aspects specific to the LinkML-Java runtime are kept isolated within the
new template variant.

Of note, the new template variant forgoes the use of Lombok annotations
to generate the read/write accessors -- they are deemed a needless
complication. We are already generating code anyway, so generating the
read/write accessors ourselves is trivial and it avoids a two-step
generation process (when the code that is generated by LinkML must then
be passed through the Lombok annotation processor before it can finally
be used).

closes #3216

* javagen: Fix typo in org.incenp.linkml template.

oocodegen/javagen: Add option to honour slot aliases when deriving field names (#3326)

* oocodegen: Add option to honour slot aliases when naming fields.

The current behaviour of `OOCodeGenerator` is to always use the _name_
of a slot to derive the name of the corresponding field in the
object-oriented representation of a schema.

This is different from the behaviour of the Python code generator, which
uses the slot alias if it exists -- in agreement with the documentation
of the `alias` slot in LinkML meta-model, which explicitly says that,
when present, the value of the `alias` slot should be used wherever the
slot name is expected.

This commit adds a `use_aliases` option to `OOCodeGenerator` to follow
the behaviour of the Python code generator (and of the spec). For
backwards compatibility, that option is set to False by default, so the
current behaviour is preserved.

A new `--use-aliases` option is added to the command-line interface of
the Java generator.

closes #3323

* javagen: Use slot aliases when present.

The LinkML runtime must know the "name" of the slot **as it appears in
instance data**. Which means that if a slot has an alias, and that alias
differs from the field name, then it is the alias that we must provide
to the Java runtime.

automatically propagates down to every subcommand.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(generators): add TypeDB 3.x TypeQL schema generator

Adds `TypeDBGenerator` (gen-typedb CLI) that converts a LinkML schema
into a TypeQL `define` block for TypeDB 3.x databases.

Mapping:
- LinkML class → TypeDB entity type
- Scalar slot → attribute type + owns declaration
- Object-ranged slot → relation type + plays declarations
- Enum → string attribute with permitted-values comment
- is_a → sub keyword; abstract → @hc59ddd3f7ba697a4 annotation
- identifier → @h2c70e12b7a0646f9; required singular → @h8367cd66fdd136bb(1..1); multivalued → @h8367cd66fdd136bb(0..)

Key implementation details:
- SchemaView-based (uses_schemaloader=False), no Jinja2 template
- Pre-computes globally-unique TypeDB labels (entity/attribute/relation
  labels must not collide); appends -attr or -rel suffixes when needed
- Handles TypeDB reserved keywords (entity, role, type, …)
- Filters inherited slots so subtypes don't redeclare already-owned attrs
- Tested against organization.yaml (unit) and dismech.yaml (live TypeDB)

Files added:
- packages/linkml/src/linkml/generators/typedbgen.py
- tests/linkml/test_generators/test_typedbgen.py (19 unit tests)
- tests/linkml/test_generators/test_typedbgen_integration.py (5 integration tests)

Verifies end-to-end that Disease entities from the dismech knowledge base
can be inserted into a TypeDB 3.x database and queried back.

- Inserts 5 smallest disorder YAML files as Disease entities
- Parametrized per-disease roundtrip test (name as @h2c70e12b7a0646f9 lookup)
- Uses module-scoped fixture so schema loads once for all 7 tests

Also documents TypeDB 3.x fetch constraint: entity variables cannot be
fetched directly; must use attribute projection ($d.name or has name $n).

subject: feat: add C++ header generator (gen-cpp-header) (#3332)
message:
feat: add C++ header generator (gen-cpp-header) (#3332)

* feat: add C++ header generator (gen-cpp-header)

New generator that produces idiomatic C++17 header files from LinkML
schemas. Follows the same architecture as the Go generator — extends
OOCodeGenerator, uses SchemaView and Jinja2 templates.

Supported features:
- enum class with to_string/from_string helpers
- struct with public inheritance from is_a
- std::optional<T> for optional fields, std::vector<T> for multivalued
- Topological ordering (base before derived)
- Automatic #include tracking
- Doxygen comments from descriptions
- Configurable namespace, template overrides

CLI: gen-cpp-header schema.yaml [--namespace X] [--alphabetical-sort]

* fix: keep structs in topological order when alphabetical sort is enabled

C++ requires types to be declared before use. Alphabetical sorting now
only applies to enums. Structs always stay in topological order so base
classes are declared before derived classes.

* test: fix formatting and improve coverage for C++ generator

Fix ruff format violations that were failing the quality-checks CI job.
Add 22 tests covering ifabsent parsing, mixins, cycle detection,
default values, custom templates, Includes operations, and build
result merging — bringing cppgen coverage from ~48% to ~98%.

* fix: address code review feedback on C++ generator

- Fix includes.strip() in module.h.jinja to use Jinja's |trim filter
  (includes is already a rendered string at template evaluation time)
- Remove unused and buggy upper_snake filter from template.py
- Fix CLI command name from cpp-header to gen-cpp-header to match
  pyproject.toml entry point

test(docgen): isolate #3242 regression in its own schema fixture

The previous commit added LeukocyteLoincCodes to kitchen_sink.yaml, which
broke 16 unrelated tests that depend on kitchen_sink's exact shape (snapshot
comparisons in markdowndatadictgen, jsonldcontextgen, gen_yaml/python/jsonld;
hardcoded counts in javagen; lifecycle filters in jsonschemagen that skip
"enum" but not dynamic enums).

Move the fixture to tests/linkml/test_generators/input/linkml_issue_3242.yaml
and add a dedicated test_docgen_dynamic_enum_include_minus test, leaving
kitchen_sink untouched.
